title: refactor(lifecycle): single permission-check library; accept user-private-group configs
body:
## Summary

Lifecycle mode-bit checks were hand-written in several modules with different rules. `cleanup.py` rejected `repos.json` on `st_mode & 0o022`, so on Ubuntu/Debian (user-private groups, `umask 002`) a `0664` config owned by the user and their private group stopped cleanup with `unsafe-repository-config`, while `filesystem.py` already accepted exactly that case for directories. The same rule was also copied inline in `enrollment.py`.

This PR adds `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/permissions.py` as the single home for ownership/mode-bit decisions:

| Function | Rule |
|---|---|
| `user_private_group(gid)`, `no_extended_access_acl(target)` | moved unchanged from `filesystem.py` |
| `is_private_mode(info)` | no group/other bits |
| `group_write_is_private(target, info)` | owned + user-private group + no POSIX access ACL |
| `shared_writable(target, info)` | other-write, or group-write that is not private |
| `read_owned_file(path, FilePolicy(reason, max_size, private, single_link=True))` | `O_NOFOLLOW` read of a bounded regular file owned by the user; raises `FilesystemValidationError(reason)` with a `violation` (`wrong-type`, `wrong-owner`, `multiple-links`, `too-large`, `not-private`, `shared-writable`) |

`FilesystemValidationError` moved to `permissions.py` and is re-exported from `filesystem.py`, so existing imports are unchanged. `filesystem.py` keeps only the path-chain checks (`checked_directory`, `validate_private_path`, sealed-ancestor rule). `bundle.py` registers the new module.

Call sites switched:
- `cleanup._repository_entries` → `read_owned_file(..., REPOSITORY_CONFIG)` (`private=False`). **Behaviour change:** user-private-group write is accepted; shared groups, other-write and ACLs are still refused.
- `enrollment._git_directory` → `shared_writable` (identical rule, local wrappers removed).
- `enrollment._read_marker` → `read_owned_file(..., MARKER_POLICY)` (`private=True, single_link=False`; identical rule).
- `archive_path.validate_archive_path`, `filesystem.validate_private_path`, `filesystem._group_write_is_private` → shared predicates (identical rules).

Reason codes are unchanged.

Out of scope: owner-only checks on worktree paths (`legacy_inventory.py`, `legacy_options.py`), `/proc` UID checks (`linux.py`), the retirement lock identity check, and shell-side permission checks in `.agents/scripts/`.

title: GH#36921: fix(lifecycle): bounded admission contention wait; release writer during PR lookups
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36921

Worker startup was failing with `admission-denied reason=OperationalError code=database-locked category=contention` (exit 75). This PR fixes the remaining writer holder that #36963 left open, and lets admission wait out short contention within a fixed limit. It does not fail open.

1. **Reconstructible legacy cleanup no longer holds the registry writer during GitHub lookups.** Each item ran two `open_pull_requests` lookups inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and each lookup makes at least two `gh api` calls.
   - The plan lookup now releases the writer. That plan is only written to the journal.
   - The refresh fetches PRs without the writer. It then reacquires the writer and re-runs every check (registry/inventory, managed authority, Git state, `/proc` census) before the non-forced `git worktree remove`.
   - Native removal still runs under the writer.
2. **Admission retries writer contention, up to a limit.** `within_contention_deadline` (policy in `ContentionWait`) repeats the whole idempotent `AdmissionRegistry.admit` transaction:
   - It retries only on `sqlite3.OperationalError` with category `contention`.
   - The default limit is 30 s. `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS` can set 0–300; an invalid value denies launch.
   - Every retry checks again that the generation is open, under the writer.
   - If an earlier attempt committed, the retry replays as `False`, which the launcher already treats as `replay-is-not-execution-authority`.
   - Each retry logs a sanitized `admission-retry` line. Contention past the limit exits 75, as before.

The SQLite busy timeout (`storage.py`, 2 s) is unchanged.

## Lock holder and timings (disposable multi-process reproduction)

Setup: a throwaway fixture repository and private registry. A separate monitor process polled `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (timeout 0) every 20 ms. A second separate process tried an admission-equivalent writer with the production 2 s timeout during each PR lookup. The simulated lookup latency was 2.3 s, taken from read-only measurements of `open_pull_requests` against this repository: 2.22 s, 2.31 s and 3.92 s.

| Scenario | Longest continuous writer hold | Admission writer during lookup |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, first item with restore probe | 4.866 s | denied `database-locked` `category=contention` after 2.008 s / 2.014 s |
| `main`, later item (probe verified) | 4.876 s | denied after 2.006 s / 2.015 s |
| this PR, first item with restore probe | 0.183 s | acquired after 0.000 s (both lookups) |
| this PR, later item | 0.171 s | acquired after 0.000 s (both lookups) |

The holder is the `process_reconstructible` writer transaction. On `main` it covers both lookups plus the local checks. With measured lookup latency each item blocks admission for about 4.4–7.8 s, which is longer than the 2 s busy timeout. No live registry was read or changed, no process was force-terminated, and nothing was deployed.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`:
  - renamed `archive_io` to `writer_released`
  - added `released_pull_requests` and `prefetched_pull_requests`
  - `legacy_plan`/`managed_plan` folded into `plan_reconstructible`, which receives the lookup to use
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/admission.py`: `ContentionWait`, `within_contention_deadline` and `contention_deadline`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch.py`: `run_admitted` uses the limited retry and logs `admission-retry`
- Tests:
  - `tests/test_reconstructible.py`: lookups do not block unrelated admission; registration during the final lookup blocks removal; a failed writer reacquisition keeps the source and a retry succeeds
  - `tests/test_admission.py`: short contention recovers, long contention fails closed, a close during contention wins, a lost acknowledgement replays without authority, non-contention errors are not retried, wait configuration stays in range
  - `tests/test_admitted_launch.py`: a writer held 3 s by a separate process lets the command run exactly once; contention past the limit exits 75 with a sanitized reason; a close committed by the competing writer never runs
  - `tests/test_legacy_cleanup.py`: rename only
  - `tests/test_reconstructible.py` (`test_unremoved_probe_can_retry_after_head_changes`): the `reconstructible` spy forwards keyword arguments
- `LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`, `REGISTRY.md`: document the writer release and the admission wait

## Decisions

- GitHub state was never serialized by SQLite, so releasing the writer during the lookup weakens no guarantee. All registry, Git and `/proc` evidence that permits removal is still checked under the writer, after the fetch.
- The admission retry is limited and covers contention only. Schema, capacity, permission, closed-generation and payload conflicts still deny immediately.
- Not changed: the one-time per-host restore probe (`verify_reconstructible(probe=True)`) still runs under the writer. It happens once per host and has its own crash recovery. Current-generation retirement (`retirement.py`) already uses short transactions.

## Summary

Give overdue synchronous blocker recovery an admission opportunity before dispatch can consume the remaining non-reserved cycle budget. Fresh-cache and asynchronous cycles retain their existing dispatch-first ordering.

## Evidence and cause

## Changes and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`: reuse `_pulse_blocker_refresh_starved`, the existing housekeeping lock and `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup` for an early recovery attempt. Wrap the entire attempt in the existing `run_stage_with_timeout` with a 180-second watchdog budget, subject to the caller's smaller ceiling and the normal cycle clamp. title: GH#37181: fix(lifecycle): memoise takeover open-PR lookups per pass; report gh deferral
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37181.

The managed takeover from #37036 (v3.39.135) ran a full open-PR lookup, `gh api repos/{slug}` plus a paginated pulls call, for every modern worktree's precheck, again for its journaled plan, and again before removal. On the shared runners the pulse's `gh` governor deferred that burst with exit 75. Every candidate was retained as `CalledProcessError` (67 and 93 per pass), so `retired=0`.

- `pull_requests.PassPullRequests` is a per-pass memo per slug. A failed lookup, including a governor deferral, is remembered for the pass and raised as `pull-request-state-unavailable`. It still holds and never proves absence.
- `CleanupOptions.pull_requests` gives each `run` a fresh memo (non-compared, grants no authority).
- In `legacy_cleanup`, the takeover precheck, preview plan and journaled plan use the memo. `prefetched_pull_requests`, the check immediately before removal, always refreshes, so removal still rests on current GitHub state (GH#36851, GH#36921). The writer is still released for every lookup.

Per pass, the cost drops from about 2 × candidates lookups to one per slug plus one per actual removal (capped by the pass `limit`).

## Verification

- `env PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_legacy_cleanup`: 76 tests OK, 1 skipped (Linux-only `/proc` test; Linux CI is authoritative).

title: GH#37222: fix: declare handoff PR issue identity in body
body:
## Problem

The pulse planning-sync protected-branch handoff pushed its branch successfully but could never
open the handoff PR. `gh_create_pr` was rejected by the `origin:worker` identity guard:

```
[SAFETY] worker PR body has ambiguous or missing explicit issue identity; keep one standalone `For #N` line; move other references under `## Related`.
[pulse-wrapper] ... status=protected_branch_publication_deferred repo=marcusquinn/aidevops wake=handoff_recovery
```

The guard reads the **body** (`gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:262-275`). The generated body had no
issue reference the extractor could see: the HTML comment marker is skipped (`:182-183`), and
`## Related issues` matches the secondary-heading pattern and is skipped too (`:190`, `:193`). The
issue number existed only in the PR **title**, which the guard never inspects.

Publication therefore deferred on every cycle and never converged.

## Impact

- 157 recorded deferrals, one per pulse cycle.
- 95 abandoned `aidevops/pulse-todo-*` branches on the public remote.
- Each deferred cycle created and discarded a full workspace clone, feeding the recovery-bucket
  growth tracked in #37214.

## Change

Emit one standalone `For #N` line in the primary body section, reusing `issue_num` — the identity
already chosen for the title at `pulse-todo-publication.sh:124`. A planning handoff closes no
issue, so the declaration is deliberately non-closing (`For`, not `Resolves`), and the linkage list
stays under its current heading so it remains excluded as secondary.

Second, `issue_num` is now validated. Its extraction pipeline ends in `sed`, which succeeds on
empty input, so a linkage with no `#N` would previously have produced a `GH#:` title and a bare
`For #` body. An absent identity now fails the handoff explicitly.

## Verification

Focused harness against the real extractor, confirming the behaviour change at the exact gate that
was rejecting the create:

```
PASS  old body (no For line)       explicit_issues=[]
PASS  new body (For #20307)        explicit_issues=[20307]
PASS  new body, single linkage     explicit_issues=[20307]
```

`shellcheck` clean. Pre-commit ratchets (return statements, positional parameters, string
literals, portable stat) and pre-push gates (secretlint, typecheck, quality) passed.

**Gate limitation, declared rather than worked around:** the repository's own
`.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh` cannot execute on this host. It aborts at
exit 127 before any assertion because it hardcodes `/usr/bin/git`, which does not exist on NixOS:

```
.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh: line 19: /usr/bin/git: No such file or directory
```

That portability defect spans 65 files and is filed separately as #37224, with `command -v -p git`
identified as the portable replacement that preserves the tests' native-Git intent. No test
isolation boundary was weakened and no host-path shim was added for this PR.

## Related

Reported in #37222. Consequences tracked separately in #37214 (recovery-bucket growth) and #37224
(Git path portability). Cleanup of the 95 existing abandoned remote branches is an operator
decision and is not part of this change.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified. Node 24.22.1, OpenCode 1.19.5.

  hooks with a scratch bus/entity DB and a deterministic loopback model endpoint
  (no external inference). Unverified asks waited idle and appeared framed
  unverified in the active session transcript. A verified-owner ask waited with
  opt-in off, then woke the recipient after `chat-wake on`. Injection exited 1;

  2 intermittent failures: unchanged MCP Playwright artifact fixture ENOENT and
  existing bus test's ordering assertion when two messages share one millisecond.
  Both pass in isolated runs; no non-chat delivery/order behavior was changed.
  Confirmed pre-existing against archived default branch `231127fce`: selected
  unchanged tests reproduced the same Playwright ENOENT (4/4) and same
  millisecond-order assertion (2/4). These are not repaired in this chat task.

## Acceptance review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Scan before write, fail closed | Real scanner/entity integration tests, normalized-control-character canary, missing scanner dependency denial, live CLI refusal |
| Verified actor/owner, negative app/channel | Exact confirmed-link fixtures, suggested/different app/different channel negatives, no-actor display-name negative |

title: t18905: message pulse workers over the session bus and relay issue steering
body:
## Summary

Same-user headless workers become session-bus endpoints. send/ask reach a worker at its next tool result or turn; workers are never woken and get no poll timer and no aidevops_sessions tool. New `aidevops sessions reply <msg-id>` answers an ask from a session shell; `--sender <label>` names a sessionless sender (origin cli:<label>, own rate key). Worker presence carries dispatch facts (issue, repo, attempt, tier, start) and the running tool; list/show label workers [worker]. notify-when-idle on a worker fires once on idle or exit. New deferrable pulse stage worker_bus_relay (.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh) sends a live worker one pointer per maintainer comment batch, closure, hold-for-review or status:claimed on its issue: pointers only (comment ID, author, gh read command), collaborator authors only, no GitHub writes, every read budget-gated; AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BUS_RELAY=0 disables it. The plan non-goal 'workers cannot be messaged' is replaced per the owner's decision (decision log 2026-11-09).



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-compaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-plugin.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence-store.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md, todo/tasks/t18905-brief.md

## Decisions

Workers are never woken and get no tool, so there is no schema cost. Pulse messages are pointers, never instructions or copied comment text; GitHub stays the system of record and hung workers stay with the watchdog. The relay is a deferrable optional stage so it never spends critical API budget. Sends to an exact session ID still queue for a non-live session (existing t18886 behaviour; worker continuations can resume). Interactive visibility of workers in who/overlap notices continues under t18895 (GH#37248).

## Runtime Testing

- macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at b3d834d87e643f98e08326bbab36a81adaf4b1cf.

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Plugin suite (npm test): 1373 tests, 1366 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped; session-bus and v2 suites 32/32 including the new worker tests. test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh and test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh (new order asserts 11e2/11e3) pass. ShellCheck clean; complexity-regression function-complexity and nesting-depth checks exit 0. Live: an isolated worker-mode opencode run (1.19.5, this branch's plugin, stub model) published headless presence with the worker block and tool=bash, received a sessionless ask --sender pulse appended to its next bash result with worker framing, had no aidevops_sessions among its 17 tools, and answered with aidevops sessions reply from its own shell; ask --wait printed the reply (rc 0) and presence was removed on exit. A live relay run against GitHub with a seeded worker record delivered one status:claimed pointer and sent nothing on re-run.

Resolves #37298
